title: Intentional Homicides in Mexico Have Fallen 51% Since September 2024
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by Fernanda Monroy originally appeared in the[August 11, 2026
edition of Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/homicidios-
dolosos-bajan-51-desde-septiembre-de-2024-sesnsp), a Mexican investigative
journalism magazine._

**The daily average of intentional homicides in Mexico dropped 51 percent
between September 2024 and July 2026, going from 86.9 to 42.5 cases per day**
, reported the head of the Executive Secretariat of the National Public
Security System (SESNSP), Marcela Figueroa Franco, who noted that this past
month recorded the lowest level since the start of the current administration.

In presenting the Crime Incidence Report, prepared with information from the
prosecutor's offices of the 32 states and figures consolidated as of July 31,
she detailed that there are currently 44 fewer intentional homicides each day
compared with September 2024.

![President Sheinbaum beside a chart of the daily homicide average from
September 2024 to July 2026](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-11-homicides-51-sesnsp-body-monthly.jpg)The
daily homicide average fell 51% between September 2024 and July 2026. Photo:
Presidencia

The official emphasized that July 2026 also recorded the lowest daily homicide
average for a month of July in the last 12 years, when comparing the
corresponding data for that month since 2015.

The reduction is also observed when the comparison is broadened to the first
seven months of each year. Between January and July 2026, an average of 48.6
intentional homicides per day was reported, the lowest figure for that period
since 2016.

In presenting the evolution of this crime over the last four presidential
terms, the head of the SESNSP indicated that during the term of Felipe
Calderón—from 2006 to 2012—the daily average of intentional homicides rose 148
percent, while between 2012 and 2018, under former president Enrique Peña
Nieto, the increase was 42 percent.

By contrast, during the administration of former president Andrés Manuel López
Obrador—from 2018 to 2024—a reduction of 9 percent was recorded. For the
current administration, the Secretariat compared the average of 91.7 daily
homicides recorded during 2024 with the 48.6 preliminarily reported between
January and July 2026, which represents a decrease of 47 percent.

![President Sheinbaum beside a chart of the daily homicide average across the
last four administrations, 2006–2026](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-11-homicides-51-sesnsp-body-sexenio.jpg)The
daily homicide average across the last four administrations, 2006–2026. Photo:
Presidencia

Regarding the distribution by state, seven states accounted for 49 percent of
the intentional homicides recorded in the country between January and July
2026, according to the report presented by the agency's head.

Guanajuato concentrated 8.6 percent of the national total, followed by Baja
California, with 8.2 percent; Chihuahua, with 8.1 percent; Sinaloa, with 7.1
percent; the State of Mexico, with 6 percent; Guerrero, with 5.6 percent; and
Morelos, with 5.5 percent.

However, comparing the first seven months of 2026 with the same period of
2025, 30 states recorded a decrease in their daily average of intentional
homicides, according to the SESNSP. In percentage terms, the official
highlighted the declines observed in San Luis Potosí, Nayarit, Quintana Roo,
and Zacatecas.

Among the states with the highest concentration of homicides, Guanajuato went
from an average of 12.7 daily cases in February 2025 to 3.1 in July of this
year, a reduction of 76 percent.

In Baja California, the average went from 7.1 daily homicides in September
2024 to 3.7 in July 2026, a decrease of 48 percent; while in the State of
Mexico it fell from 6.6 to 2.7 daily cases since the start of the current
administration, equivalent to a reduction of 59 percent.

In Guerrero, the daily average dropped from 6.6 to 2.5 homicides between the
beginning of the administration and July of this year, a reduction of 61
percent, according to the data presented.

For Morelos, the official explained that the average remained relatively
stable during the first 20 months of the administration, but fell from 4.3 to
2.1 daily homicides since the implementation of the Morelos Plan three months
ago, which represents a decrease of 51 percent.

In Sinaloa, where the official attributed the increase in violence recorded
since September 2024 to a dispute between organized crime groups, the average
went from 6.9 daily homicides in June 2025—when it reached its highest
point—to 3.3 in July 2026.

This represents a reduction of 52 percent, while July became the second month
with the lowest daily homicide average in the state over the past year.

Likewise, the head of the SESNSP reported the downward trend that also
appeared in high-impact crimes, whose daily average fell 33 percent between
October 2024 and July 2026.

She detailed that in October 2024 an average of 636.6 high-impact crimes per
day were recorded nationally, while in July of this year the figure stood at
424.4 cases, the lowest monthly level of the last 22 months analyzed.

In particular, vehicle theft with violence recorded a decrease of 54 percent
between September 2024 and July 2026. This past month also posted the lowest
daily average for this crime since the beginning of the current
administration.

Comparing the first seven months of 2026 with the same period of 2025, the
SESNSP reported reductions in the various high-impact crimes included in the
report.

In addition, there was a reduction in the crime of femicide, which fell 7.7
percent; intentional injuries from firearm discharge, 11.4 percent;
kidnapping, 28.2 percent; and total robberies with violence, 15.9 percent.
